blocks.text:
Travel to the archaeological site of Quiriguá. The ancient Maya city was founded by settlers from Copán in the second half of the seventh century.

Quiriguá Archaeological Park is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. During excavations among the tropical trees, 22 carved stelae and monuments were discovered.

Among the finds are sculptures of animals with human features, thought to depict deities. Some of these monolithic sculptures weigh up to 65 tonnes and were made without iron tools. As Quiriguá was established by people from Copán, these two days reveal two connected Maya centres on opposite sides of today’s border.

After the visit, continue to Flores. This journey sets the scene for the final archaeological part of the itinerary, devoted to Tikal and the northern Petén region.

**Hotel:** Villa Maya.  
**Meals:** breakfast.

blocks.text:
Tikal is approximately 64 km from Flores, a town on an island in Lake Petén Itzá.

The name Tikal is translated as “the place where the voices of spirits are heard”. The city was inhabited from around 800 BC to AD 900 before the jungle gradually reclaimed it.

The central part of the complex covers about 16 sq km and contains approximately 3,000 structures. Six pyramid temples stand out above the rest. The extent of the buildings and the number of structures make Tikal comparable in scale to a major city of the ancient world.

Tikal National Park covers approximately 575 sq km. In 1979 it was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List as both a cultural and natural site. More than at the previous archaeological complexes, here you see monumental architecture rising directly out of the tropical forest: ancient temples emerge above the canopy, while much of the site remains part of the natural park.

In the afternoon, transfer to Flores Airport for a domestic flight to Guatemala City.

**Hotel:** Barceló Guatemala City.  
**Meals:** breakfast.
